posix.title: When Prompts Vary but Intent Remains: Enforcing Robustness in Vision Language Models

problems.name: Hidden reasons
problems.blurb: A model's stated explanation is not always the reason behind its answer.

problems.name: Unmeasured persuasion
problems.blurb: There is no standard way to measure how well a model talks people round, or how that changes once it is trained to.

problems.name: Judges swayed by persuasion
problems.blurb: A judge model can be won over by rhetoric rather than evidence, so persuasive answers get rewarded over true ones.

problems.name: Fakes passing as real
problems.blurb: Generated images and audio pass as authentic, and a detector trained on yesterday's generators misses tomorrow's.

problems.name: Hidden orders in pages
problems.blurb: A web page can carry an instruction that an agent reads and follows as if it came from the user.

problems.name: Scarce injection examples
problems.blurb: Real injection attacks are rare and adaptive, so there is little data to train a defence on.

problems.name: Self-changing agents
problems.blurb: An agent that rewrites its own strategy can drift away from what it was deployed to do.

problems.name: Steered activations
problems.blurb: Nudging a model's internal activations can plant a bias that no prompt filter ever sees.

problems.name: Oversharing agents
problems.blurb: An agent with access to private context can reveal it to the wrong party in the course of a task.

problems.name: Failures real users find
problems.blurb: Real users make typos, change the format, paraphrase, push back and go off-script, and a model's answer should not change when only the wording does. Benchmarks miss these failures; prompt-variation tests and live deployments find them.

problems.name: Missed medical findings
problems.blurb: Segmentation models trained on one population miss tumours in scans from another, and adapting them is costly.

problems.name: Distracted robot vision
problems.blurb: Navigation models lose their way when the instruction changes language or the scene gets cluttered.
papers: Language and Planning in Robotic Navigation

problems.name: Overconfident models
problems.blurb: Models rarely notice when they are out of their depth, so they neither abstain nor escalate.

problems.name: Vendor-locked GPU code
problems.blurb: CUDA code is tied to one vendor's accelerators, and porting it to another by hand is slow and error-prone.

problems.name: Unverified assembly translation
problems.blurb: A translated binary that assembles is not one that behaves the same, so translation needs test-backed guarantees.

problems.name: Agents that never learn
problems.blurb: A deployed recommendation agent keeps the same strategy while demand shifts under it.
